decisions.issues: Minor only: a lit brass oil lamp stands in the lower-left foreground of a daylight building site (harmless, open wick, period-correct). Otherwise on beat: laterite bastion with lashed bamboo scaffolding, labourers hauling blocks up an earth ramp, bare-chested Nair musketeers in white mundu and topknots with muskets shouldered, no coats or hats, flat bright sea with no sail. No text. Both captions fit in the open sky at upper right.

Clean. Yusuf reads correctly: lean, white skullcap, neatly trimmed dark beard, dark short sea coat over a white tunic, no turban, no scar, so he is distinct from Ibrahim. He leans over a table piled with cloth, half-smiling, eyes sliding to the side. The market has palm-thatch awnings, open pepper sacks and a brass scale with coins in one pan. Hands are sound. A temple tower in the far background is plausible for south Travancore. Caption space: the thatch band at top left and the sky patch at top right.

Clean. The priest matches the V13 temple-priest sheet: curly hair, white forehead lines with a red dot, sacred thread, gold-bordered white cloth, and an unreadable downcast face. The stout merchant in fine bordered cloth bows low and drops a single silver coin into the brass offering tray. Brass oil-lamp stands light a mandapam at dusk. Hands are sound. The caption fits in the dusk sky at upper left.

Acceptable, with small flaws. On Nagoji's inner left forearm the brand is a tiny dark reddish rosette rather than a pale puckered patch. It is not legible and not a cross, and the long white scar is correct. A faint grey jaw shadow shows, but he reads as clean-shaven. The palm leaf carries a few faint stylus scratches that will not read at print size. Everything else is on lock: black topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, plain cream mundu with no gold border and a shoulder cloth, ivory-handled knife at the waist, NO silver chain. Ramayyan matches his sheet and sits cross-legged among palm-leaf bundles with his stylus, under morning light through a wooden lattice. Ramayyan's balloons fit on the plain wall at upper centre between the doorway and the lattice.

Minor only. The longboat sits in the surf rather than fully run up on the sand, and its plain white pennant flies from the left (bow) end. A tiny distant sail on the horizon is plausibly the envoys' ship. The interpreter (empty-handed, coloured-border shoulder cloth) walks beside the envoys; 1.5 does not name him, but he matches the chapter bible row and 3.2. Envoys are on lock: the senior in a grey powdered wig and charcoal coat with his tricorne at his chest; the younger with his own tied-back brown hair, a brown coat and his tricorne in hand. The scribes are bareheaded clerks in grey coats wading with ribbon-tied paper bundles. No blue coats, soldiers or drums, and the bastion matches 1.1. The caption fits in the open sky at upper left.

v01 fails the script beat. The Dutch party is drawn twice: once as silhouettes in the far doorway, which is correct, and again as fully rendered figures in the near right foreground, seated among the ministers. These are the wigged senior envoy seen from behind, the brown-coated younger envoy, a grey-coated clerk and an attendant. The script says the Dutch appear ONLY as backlit silhouettes at the far end. Foreground envoys also contradict 2.3, where the senior envoy is still walking up the hall. Smaller faults: Nagoji carries a long sword-like weapon at his hip instead of the short ivory-handled conch-mark knife, and he wears a small drop earring rather than a stud. Everything else is good: the hall, Varma's turban and crest, Ramayyan with leaves and stylus, Padmini and Revathi on the left, and Nagoji's black topknot, chain, moustache and clean chin.
decisions.correction: Remove every European figure from the foreground and mid-ground. There must be no wigged envoy, no brown-coated young man, no grey-coated clerk and no foreign attendant in the near right corner or among the seated courtiers. Fill the right foreground instead with bareheaded ministers in plain white cloth seated cross-legged, seen from behind or in profile. Show the Dutch party ONLY as two or three small, dark, featureless backlit silhouettes standing in the bright glare of the far doorway behind the king, as already drawn there, with no readable faces. Keep the hall, the pillars, the brass lamps, Marthanda Varma on his low platform with his crested cream-and-gold turban and spear, Ramayyan at the foot of the platform, and Padmini and Revathi seated on the left exactly as they are. Nagoji stays the only standing man beside the platform, on the king's right. He has a black topknot, a bare chest under the plain cream shoulder cloth, a heavy silver chain of office with a round silver pendant, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold ear stud (a stud, not a drop earring). Instead of a long sword at his hip, he wears only a short ivory-handled knife tucked into the waist of his plain cream mundu. Keep a plain band of shadowed wall or rafters across the top left for two caption boxes.

decisions.issues: Minor issues; acceptable. The shoulder cloth carries a gold stripe, where the script stresses plain cream with no gold border. The chain is drawn as linked oval plaques with a conch pendant, while 2.1 and 2.3 show plain heavy links with a round pendant, so it varies across the page. Otherwise the beat is correct: a heavy silver chain across the cream shoulder cloth, the ivory hilt with the conch mark at the lower edge, and a clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache and gold ear stud at the top edge. There is no text. Both captions fit on the plain cream cloth at the lower left and the rafters and sky at the upper right.

Minor issues; acceptable. Nagoji's hair has a knot on the crown, but long curly locks still hang down behind it, and the grey at his temple is a little stronger than a 'first touch'. The senior envoy's lace jabot and cuff ruffles are fuller than the 'thin lace' the script asks for. The chain is plain heavy links with a round pendant, not the plaque chain of the 2.2 insert. The beat reads clearly: the wigged, heavy-lidded senior envoy holds his tricorne to his chest and slides his eyes toward Nagoji's chain, and the anxious younger envoy, with his own brown hair tied back and in a brown coat, follows the look. Nagoji is cropped at the right edge with no turban, a moustache, a clean chin and an ear stud. There is no text. The caption fits in the clear sky between the envoy's wig and Nagoji.

The foreground is good. Lannoy is seen from behind in the white tunic-coat and mundu, matching his sheet, with pale hair tied back and the cloth-wrapped sword hilt. Two Nair guards stand beside him, the senior envoy dips a stiff bow and the younger envoy is open-mouthed. The far end of the hall, at the centre of the frame, breaks the bible and the page blocking. Varma wears a gold CROWN or helmet (the bible says never a crown) and sits on a high-backed chair-throne instead of the low platform. A turbaned attendant with a spear stands beside him where Nagoji, the only standing man, should be, with no turban. A bearded man sits at the foot of the platform in Ramayyan's place. Two women in cream saris sit up on the platform beside the king, instead of Padmini and Revathi (indigo) seated on the left of the hall.
decisions.correction: Keep the foreground exactly as drawn: Lannoy from behind at frame right in the white tunic-coat and white mundu with the cloth-wrapped sword hilt and pale hair tied with a black ribbon, the two Nair guards beside him, and the two envoys stopped in the aisle, the senior bowing with his tricorne at his chest and the younger open-mouthed. Fix the far end of the hall. Marthanda Varma sits on a LOW platform with his bare feet on a woven mat, NOT on a high-backed chair. He wears a cream-and-gold TURBAN with a jewelled peacock-feather crest, never a gold crown or helmet, and is bare-chested in cream-and-gold cloth with gold necklaces, his spear leaning beside him rather than held by anyone. The ONLY standing man beside the platform is Nagoji, on the king's right. He has black hair in a topknot, NO turban, a bare chest with a plain cream shoulder cloth, a heavy silver chain of office, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, and no spear. Remove the turbaned spear-bearer. Ramayyan, thin and clean-shaven with receding hair, in plain white cloth, sits cross-legged low at the foot of the platform; there is no bearded man there. Put no women on or beside the platform. Padmini Amma (cream sari, black hair threaded with grey and coiled at the nape, long walking stick) and Revathi Bayi (deep indigo sari with gold) sit together on the floor on the left side of the hall among the seated ministers. Keep the rafters and the sky at the upper left clear above the envoys for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor issues; acceptable. The framing is a waist-up medium shot rather than a tight close-up, and his eyeline goes off screen right. Lannoy matches his sheet: pale wavy hair tied back with a black ribbon, no wig, a white tunic-coat over an open-collared shirt and the cloth-wrapped sword hilt. He stands calm and unreadable at a carved pillar at the hall's edge, which matches the blocking, in the same open coastal hall as 2.3 and 2.4. There is no text. Both balloons fit in the open rafters and sky on the left half.

v01 shows the beat correctly: Lannoy in his white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals walks out at frame right, the senior and younger envoys and the grey-coated scribes face the platform from behind, and Varma (turban, peacock crest, cream and gold, necklaces) sits still. The hall around the platform breaks the blocking set for pages 2 to 7 and does not match 2.1. Nagoji is missing: in his place on the king's right a bare-chested spearman with a shield stands beside the platform. The man seated at the platform's foot, where Ramayyan sits, is fully bald with a thick moustache, but Ramayyan's sheet has curly side hair and no moustache. Two young women in red and green saris sit beside the platform on the viewer's right. Neither matches Padmini (fifties, cream sari, stick), who is in the foreground of 3.5, or Revathi (indigo). In 2.1 both sit on the viewer's left. A reader would take these women for the hall's two principal women in the wrong dress. Lettering space is fine (roof band and sky), and the panel has no painted text.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, the open seaward hall, the daylight, the envoys and grey-coated scribes seen from behind at frame left, the interpreter with the red-and-gold-bordered shoulder cloth in the centre foreground, Lannoy in his white tunic-coat, white mundu and sandals stepping out at frame right, and Varma perfectly still on his platform with eyes slightly narrowed. Fix only the people around the platform so they match the hall blocking of pages 2 to 7. The ONLY man standing beside the platform is Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai), close on the king's right, which is the viewer's LEFT of Varma. He has BLACK hair in a Kerala topknot with a first touch of grey at the temples, NO turban, a plain cream mundu with a shoulder cloth, the heavy silver chain of office across his chest, the ivory-handled knife at his waist, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold ear stud. Put NO spear-and-shield guard beside the platform; palace guards stand only at the outer pillars. Seated cross-legged low at the foot of the platform is Ramayyan: thin, with sharp fine features, CLEAN-SHAVEN with NO moustache, a bald crown with curly black hair at the sides, plain white cloth, a palm-leaf bundle and a stylus. Put NO women beside the platform and NO red or green saris anywhere. Padmini Amma (fifties, black hair with grey threads coiled at the nape, cream sari with a narrow gold border, long walking stick) and Revathi Bayi (deep indigo-blue sari with gold, jasmine in her braid) sit on the viewer's LEFT side of the hall and may be mostly hidden behind the envoys' backs. The seated ministers at the right stay bareheaded in white cloth.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The two scribes write with thin pens on hand-held writing boards, which the script does not ask for but which is harmless and of the period. The senior envoy's lace cuffs are a little fuller than the 'thin trim' of 1.5. Otherwise it is clean: he bows with the tricorne pressed to his chest, and the empty-handed young interpreter in a coloured-border shoulder cloth leans in to relay. The hall, lamps and sea view match 2.1 to 2.4 and 3.1. The roof band and the sky at upper right hold the single balloon.

Minor only. A soft-focus tower building on the far shore at right reads faintly European; it can pass for a coastal bastion. Varma matches the varma-v1 sheet and the ch18 court look: cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock crest, bare chest, cream and gold cloth, gold necklaces and the spear at hand. His head is tilted and a hand rests on his knee, and both hands are sound. The large clear sky at centre takes all three balloons.

Minor only. The envoy spreads one hand palm-up while the other keeps the tricorne at his chest, not both hands. The grey-coated, bareheaded scribes clutch red-ribbon-tied paper bundles, the younger envoy and the interpreter match 3.2, and the hands and anatomy are sound. The roof band and the open sky between the centre and right pillars give room for the balloons. Ramayyan is off-panel at the platform foot, toward the right where the envoy gestures, so his tail goes to the lower right edge.

Minor. Padmini stands by a pillar, but the hall blocking has her seated with Revathi on the left and 4.5 has them seated. The grey threading the ch16 to 27 row asks for shows only faintly in her hair. The younger envoy's brown coat has gold edging that 3.4 does not show. Padmini otherwise matches her sheet (face, black hair coiled at the nape, gold earrings and necklace, cream sari with gold border in the old drape, long stick) with both hands folded on the stick head. The small background envoy beckons a scribe forward, and the hall and sea match the page. The roof band and the sky at centre and right hold the four balloons.

Minor only. The Dutch scribe offers the ribbon-tied document with one visible hand, not both. The young scribe holds a small bound stack of blank leaves rather than a single palm leaf, though it still reads as a palm-leaf bundle with stylus. Otherwise clean: Ramayyan matches his sheet and lifts two fingers without reaching; the senior envoy (grey wig, charcoal coat, tricorne), younger envoy (brown hair, brown coat), grey-coated bareheaded scribe and empty-handed interpreter all match the ch18 row; same open coastal hall with sea view as pages 2 and 3; no text. 'Read.' fits in the sky between the pillar and the palms or on the mat floor.

Minor staging inconsistency: the envoys, scribe and interpreter sit cross-legged on the mats here, while in 4.1 and 4.4 they stand. Seated envoys already appear in 2.1, and the seated scribe matches 4.3, so this is acceptable. Revathi matches her sheet and the script (profile, indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, bell earrings, sandalwood line, no tali). The paper shows only faint unreadable strokes. The senior envoy's sideways, tight-jawed look at her fits the beat. The caption fits along the dark rafters at the top. Revathi's two balloons fit in the sky and rafters between her head and the senior envoy, above the scribe.

Clean. Lannoy matches the v15b sheet and the ch16-23 row: pale curly hair tied back with a black ribbon, white stand-collar tunic-coat, cloth-wrapped sword hilt as in 2.4. He leans at the pillar with his arms folded (hands sound) and one corner of his mouth twitches. The scribe reads in the soft background, seated as in 4.2. The scribe's off line fits in the large open sky to the upper left. The tail point is the visible background scribe's mouth.

Varma is correct (V13 face, cream-and-gold turban with jewelled peacock crest, spear upright), and the envoy's back, interpreter and murmuring ministers work. Nagoji fails three ways. (1) He stands SCREEN RIGHT of Varma, on the king's LEFT, which breaks the script ('at the king's right') and the hall blocking set in 2.1, where he stands screen left of the platform. (2) He wears a thin beaded silver necklace instead of the heavy linked silver chain of office with conch medallion seen in 2.2. (3) He carries a long brass-hilted sword at his waist instead of the short ivory-handled conch-mark knife. His mundu and shoulder cloth also have broad gold borders, but the chapter look note says no gold border. His face is fine (topknot, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud).
decisions.correction: Place Nagoji on the KING'S RIGHT, which in this view looking up the hall at the seated king is SCREEN LEFT of Varma, standing close beside the platform between Varma and the left-hand pillars, exactly as in panel 2.1; nobody stands on screen right of Varma, where only the spear stands upright. Nagoji wears the HEAVY silver chain of office: broad linked flat silver plaques with a conch medallion lying across his cream shoulder cloth (as in panel 2.2), NOT a thin beaded necklace. At his waist he carries ONLY the short ivory-handled knife with the conch mark, its pale ivory hilt tucked into the mundu waist; NO sword, no long brass hilt, no long scabbard. Plain cream mundu and cream shoulder cloth with NO gold border, and first grey at the temples of his black topknot. Keep everything else as it is: the low angle, Varma's cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest and gold necklaces, the senior envoy's grey-wigged back in the near foreground with the younger envoy and interpreter, the ministers turning to murmur along both sides, the open hall with sea view, and the clear sky between the pillars for lettering.

decisions.issues: Padmini matches her sheet: coiled black hair threaded with grey, cream sari with gold border, old drape, stick, simple gold. The hall setting and lettering space (sky to the upper right, ceiling at top) are good. Revathi has a bright orange-red sindoor line painted in her hair parting. That is a married woman's mark. She is still a widow in ch18 (the script says no tali), and it does not match her sheet or her look in 2.1, where her parting is plain. Her face is also scowling with an agitated open mouth, while the script says her voice is level.
decisions.correction: Revathi's hair parting is plain black: NO sindoor, no red or orange line in the parting and no red dot, because she is a widow and wears no marriage marks; her only forehead mark is the thin pale sandalwood line at the hairline, as on her sheet and in panel 2.1. Her expression is composed and level: brows only slightly drawn, mouth just open in calm speech, not a scowl. Her face is turned toward the viewer. Keep everything else as it is: Padmini seated at left with her walking stick, grey-threaded coiled hair and cream gold-bordered sari; Revathi seated beside her, not rising, in the indigo-and-gold sari with the jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, bell earrings, gold armlets and bangles; the carved pillars, brass lamps and open sea view of the hall; and the clear sky and ceiling above and to the right of Revathi for the two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The senior envoy matches the ch18 lock (grey powdered wig, charcoal coat, black tricorne) and looks down at the hat as scripted. The younger envoy, the grey-coated scribes and the interpreter in his coloured-border cloth are all correct, and the hall matches page 4 (carved pillars, brass lamps, open to the sea). The scribes' pens are dark and cylindrical, a little like modern pens, but they are tiny at print size. Their notebooks show no writing. The open sky at upper right gives clean space for the two envoy balloons and Padmini's small off-panel balloon. Her tail points to the right edge, because in 5.3 she and Revathi sit on the envoys' left, the sea side of the hall.

Minor only. The envoy turns the tricorne idly in his fingers with a casual, heavy-lidded look off to the side, which fits the beat. His costume, the hall and the lighting match 5.1. The interpreter's hair is tied back here but loose in 5.1, a small inconsistency. The scribes' notebooks show no writing. The envoy balloons can sit in the sky gap between the centre pillars, above the ships, or along the roof band at the top.

Minor only. This is one widescreen frame in depth, as scripted. Ramayyan's stylus is stopped on his palm-leaf bundle, though it touches the bundle's top edge rather than an open leaf. His face is also in frame and matches his sheet (receding curly hair, white cloth). Revathi's hand curls into a loose fist on her knee; her indigo-and-gold sari, armlet, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace and sandal line are correct, and she wears no tali. Varma, on the far platform, frowns with narrowed eyes in the cream-and-gold turban with the peacock-feather crest. The red throne hangings behind him do not appear in 4.4 or 5.4, a small setting inconsistency. The caption fits on the plain cream wall above Varma's turban (top centre-right) or on the floor mats at bottom centre. The leaves show no writing.

Acceptable with background quibbles. The two-shot works: the envoy is near with his back half to us (wig, black bow, charcoal coat, tricorne), and Varma sits far and small on the platform, correctly turbaned and crested. The court is silent. The scribe's paper shows no writing. Two background points. Two court women by the dais wear red and green saris; they cannot be mistaken for Revathi (indigo) or Padmini (cream), but they are extra figures. A guard at the far right edge wears a dark vest over a white shirt instead of the bare-chested Nair look, but he is small and cut by the frame. Nagoji, who stood beside the king in 4.4, is not on the platform; the script does not require him here. The envoy balloons can sit in the sky at upper left; Varma's fits on the plain cream wall above his head (about x 0.57 to 0.77, y 0.22 to 0.33). The envoy's face is turned away, so his tail goes to the side of his head.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches the ch18 Ananthan Pillai lock: black topknot, no turban, grey at the temple, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, cream shoulder cloth and silver chain. His eyes are turned aside and distant. At full zoom there is light hatched shading on the chin, but it reads as clean-shaven with no beard. The grey streak at the temple is a little more prominent than 'first touch'. The soft-edged inset shows a palm leaf at a raking angle with fine, illegible incised rows, as the script asks, and the small notch at the leaf's edge is clearly the focus. There are no legible letters. The three captions fit along the top-left band over the ceiling and pillars, in the gap between his head and the inset, or on the floor at bottom left, all clear of the face and the notch. The setting matches the hall in the rest of the page.

v01 (only candidate) has the right composition but fails on four counts. (1) Pseudo-text: the red runner on the platform step, in the centre between the two envoys' heads, carries a band of glyph-like characters that read as Malayalam-style script. It sits in the key area under the king, so a balloon cannot cover it. (2) Nagoji's crossed LEFT forearm shows a raw red X-shaped double gash, which reads as a cross. The bible calls for a pale puckered brand patch with a long thin WHITE scar beside it, not a cross. (3) Nagoji's mundu and shoulder cloth have broad gold borders, but the chapter look is plain cream with NO gold border. (4) The Revathi inset shows a tightly clenched fist where the script calls for the fist from 5.3 loosening. Everything else works: Varma in turban and crest with the spear, Nagoji at the king's right with topknot, clean chin, ear stud, silver chain and ivory knife, correct envoy costumes, straight lamp flames, and the same open-sided hall as 2.1 and 6.2.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition. That means the low angle over the backs of the senior envoy (grey powdered wig, charcoal coat, black tricorne in hand) and the younger envoy (own brown hair, brown coat), Varma centred on his platform in the cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, the spear upright beside him, Nagoji standing at the king's right (screen left), straight lamp flames, the open-sided carved-pillar hall with the sea beyond, and the square inset at lower left. Fix four things. First, the red runner and every step, cushion and carpet edge carry only a plain woven stripe or simple geometric pattern: no glyphs, no letter-like or script-like shapes, no lettering of any kind anywhere in the frame. Second, Nagoji's mundu and shoulder cloth are plain cream cotton with NO gold border or coloured stripe; his only adornments are the heavy silver chain of office and the ivory-handled knife at his waist. Third, his LEFT forearm shows no red marks and no crossing lines. Either turn the inner forearm away from camera, or show only a small pale puckered patch of raised skin a hand's width above the wrist, with a single long thin WHITE scar running from the wrist toward the elbow beside it, never an X or a cross. Fourth, in the inset, Revathi's hand rests on her knee over the indigo-and-gold sari border with the fingers beginning to uncurl and open, relaxing, not a tight fist.

decisions.issues: Clean. The beat reads: Varma, seen from behind, raises his right hand palm out in the foreground (back of the hand to camera, thumb and four fingers sound), and the senior envoy has his mouth open mid-word. Varma matches his sheet (turban and peacock crest, pearl ear drops, curled moustache, bare back, gold-bordered cloth). The envoys, scribes and interpreter match the chapter 18 row. The room is the same open-sided hall with the sea beyond. Varma's mouth is hidden behind his cheek, so the tail point is at the moustache. There is wide, clear sky across the upper right for all three Varma balloons.

Acceptable, with minor deviations. Varma is framed medium-close rather than tight. Ramayyan is in sharp focus rather than soft, and his leaf bundle is closed, with the stylus paused above it. Both characters match their sheets: Varma in turban and peacock crest with gold necklaces and the spear; Ramayyan thin, with receding curly hair and plain white cloth, his eyes lifted toward the king. The hall matches the neighbouring panels. The anatomy is sound and there is no text. The open sky between the pillars at upper left takes both Varma balloons clear of the faces.

v01 (only candidate) puts a bare-chested man standing directly behind Varma on the king's right (screen left) with a shield and spear. He has a black topknot, a thick curled moustache and a small gold ear stud. That is exactly where Nagoji stands in 6.1, and the page blocking makes Nagoji the only man standing beside the platform, so readers will take this figure for Nagoji in the wrong dress: a gold necklace instead of the silver chain, a red waist sash, a red forehead mark, no shoulder cloth. The beat is also weak. Varma's eyes go screen right, toward the envoys, rather than clearly away from them toward the edge of the hall, and the senior envoy's throat working does not read. The seated bearded minister in the mid-ground wears gold chains, which the script rules out. The envoy costumes, Varma's own look, the hall and the lettering space are all fine.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition. That means Varma seated at screen left on his red-cushioned platform in the cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest; the senior envoy (grey powdered wig, charcoal coat, black tricorne held to his chest) and the younger envoy (own brown hair tied back, brown coat) at screen right with the grey-coated scribes and the interpreter; seated ministers in the mid-ground; and the open-sided carved-pillar hall with the sea beyond and clear sky at the top. Remove the standing bare-chested guard behind Varma: nobody stands beside the king in this panel, and no figure anywhere has a topknot with a thick curled moustache and a gold ear stud. Any background guards stand far back near the pillars, in white headbands like the guards in the previous panels. Make the beat unmistakable. Varma's head and eyes are turned away from the senior envoy, past him and over the envoys' shoulders toward a distant pillar at the far right edge of the hall. The senior envoy, in three-quarter view toward the king, swallows hard: lips pressed shut, throat tensed, Adam's apple visible above the lace stock. The seated ministers are bareheaded in plain white cloth with no gold chains or necklaces.

decisions.issues: v01 (only candidate) gets Lannoy right: tall, pale hair tied back, white tunic-coat, white ankle-length mundu, sandals, a cloth-wrapped sword hilt, standing straight at his pillar at screen right. But the frame is a wide shot of the whole hall, and almost everything else in it breaks continuity. Varma on the platform is bare-headed with a topknot, with no turban or crest, unlike 6.1 to 6.4. The man seated at the foot of the platform is bearded and does not read as Ramayyan. Nagoji is missing from the king's right, and a guard stands beside the platform instead. The two seated women wear green and gold saris instead of Padmini's cream and Revathi's indigo. The envoys from behind wear green, near-black and maroon coats with three powdered wigs, instead of one charcoal coat with a grey wig, one brown coat with the younger envoy's own brown hair, and grey-coated scribes.
decisions.correction: Make this a full-width bottom strip that is about Lannoy alone, not an establishing view of the hall. Keep Lannoy exactly as drawn: tall, pale wavy hair tied back with a black ribbon, no wig, plain white cotton tunic-coat with a standing collar, white ankle-length mundu, sandals, sword hung at his side with a cloth-wrapped hilt. He stands very straight against a carved wooden pillar on a laterite base at screen right, in medium shot from the knees up, his eyes fixed on a point past the envoys' shoulders. At screen left, in the soft-focus foreground, show only the backs of the two envoys' heads and shoulders as dark shapes: the senior in a grey powdered wig and a charcoal coat, the younger with his own brown hair tied back and a brown coat. No other coat colours. Do NOT show the royal platform, the king, the seated women, the ministers or the guards. The rest of the frame is the same open-sided hall as the previous panels: a brass oil-lamp stand with open wicks, palms and sea beyond the pillars, and a plain stretch of pale sky or plain wall in the upper middle left free for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only: Lannoy's hilt is brass with a knotted cloth tassel rather than a fully wrapped grip, and the scabbard hangs without a visible belt. Ramayyan, both envoys (tricornes held to the chest, the younger one looking as if he might choke, the senior one composed), Lannoy at his pillar in white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals, and the open-sided hall all match pages 2 to 6. Lettering space: the roof and rafter band at upper left, above Ramayyan, is clear.

Clean. The Dutch paper lies flat beside the tied palm-leaf bundle and stylus. It carries only faint blurred rows with nothing legible, as the script asks. Ramayyan is seated, calm, below the standing senior envoy. Lettering space: the open sky between the pillars at left and centre-left, and the roof band at top right.

Minor only: the hall behind him reads empty in this close shot, with a plain back wall at right that does not appear in earlier panels. It is plausible for this camera angle. Ramayyan matches his sheet and is writing on his leaf, with his forearm pinning the Dutch paper at the left edge. The paper's marks are faint and illegible. Hands are sound. The plain wall at right gives generous space for the three heavy balloons.

v01 (the only candidate) is rejected. The background platform at upper left shows a king who does not match Varma's sheet: a gold crown in place of the cream-and-gold turban with the peacock-feather crest, a full beard instead of a clean chin, and a covered torso on a throne chair. Two women in green and maroon saris sit on the platform beside him, which breaks Padmini's and Revathi's looks and the hall blocking. A bare-chested spearman stands where Nagoji should be. The script beat is also missed: the hall is still full rather than thinning, and the Nair guards walk away from the Dutch instead of escorting them toward the doors. Lannoy and the senior envoy are good: Lannoy in white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals at his pillar, hands behind his back; the senior envoy in grey wig and charcoal coat with his tricorne, gesturing to him.
decisions.correction: Keep Lannoy and the senior envoy exactly as drawn. Lannoy stands at the carved pillar at frame right: pale wavy hair tied back with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat, ankle-length white mundu, sandals, hands clasped behind his back, sword at his hip. The senior envoy has paused at frame left of him: grey powdered wig, charcoal coat, black tricorne held to his chest, one hand half-raised toward Lannoy. Keep the open-sided hall with carved pillars, brass lamp stands and the sea beyond, in warm late-afternoon light. The audience is OVER. The king's platform in the far background must be EMPTY: no king, no crowned or bearded figure, no throne chair, no women and no spearman on it, only the bare low platform, its mat and lamp stands. Do not show Varma, Nagoji, Padmini or Revathi anywhere. Thin the hall: only a few chiefs in white mundu walking off in pairs toward the far end, heads together, and many empty mats. At frame left, two Nair palace guards (bare-chested, white mundu, sword and round shield) walk beside the younger envoy (brown coat, his own brown hair), the grey-coated scribes and the interpreter. One guard gestures them toward the doorway, so the Dutch party is clearly being escorted out. Keep the roof and rafter band across the top and the sky above the sea low in detail for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The sky is a pale late-day blue, not the pinkish sunset of 7.4; this is acceptable, and the 7.4 regeneration is asked for matching late-afternoon light. The sword hilt here is fully cloth-wrapped, while 7.1 and 7.4 show a brass grip with a cloth knot. The script beat is met: a close two-shot in profile, the two men facing away from each other. The envoy has his grey wig, charcoal coat and thin lace cuff. Lannoy has his own pale hair tied back, the white tunic-coat and the cloth-wrapped hilt at his hip. Lettering space: the rafter band across the top and the sky and palms between the two heads.

Minor only. A thin gold hem shows on the trailing end of Nagoji's shoulder cloth, but the mundu itself is plain, so it barely touches the chapter's no-gold-border lock. The grey at his temple is one bold streak, a little more than a first touch, but the hair is clearly black and he is not the grey later-life figure. The rest matches: topknot, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, silver chain catching the light, conch-marked ivory knife. Revathi is in indigo with jasmine braid, flat coins, armlets and sandalwood line; her tiny brow dot matches her sheet. The verandah, palms, sea and low sun are right. The open sky at upper right, and the roof beams above the post, take the short balloon.

Clean apart from the flat coins catching the light only modestly, not as bright small suns. Revathi is half-turned to camera at the rail on the same verandah and in the same light as 8.1, Nagoji is not drawn, and her hands and bangles are sound. The whole sky and sea on the right half are clear for the four balloons. Nagoji's off-panel tail goes to the left edge, the direction he is coming from along the verandah.

Framing does not match the beat. The script asks for Nagoji's point of view, tight on the flat coins at her throat. v01 is a chest-up portrait whose largest element is Revathi's whole face, frowning off to frame right, with the coins as a secondary detail. It repeats 8.2 as a second face close-up and undoes the restage that made 8.3 a caption-only insert. Costume, setting and anatomy are otherwise fine.
decisions.correction: Frame this as a tight insert from Nagoji's point of view, not a portrait: the camera close on Revathi's throat and collarbone, with the necklace of flat gold coins (flat discs, not round beads) filling the centre of the frame and flashing like small, steady suns in the low late-afternoon sun. Cut the frame just below her lips so only the line of her jaw and chin shows at the top edge: no eyes, no full face. Put the edge of her black braid with jasmine at one side and the gold-bordered indigo sari across the bottom. Keep the out-of-focus warm sky and sea in the upper corner opposite the braid clear and low-detail for one caption. Same verandah light as 8.2; no tali.

decisions.issues: Nagoji's mundu and shoulder cloth have broad gold kasavu borders: two gold stripes down the front and gold along the shoulder cloth. The chapter's Ananthan Pillai lock says plain cream mundu with NO gold border (the gold-bordered later-life sheet figure is explicitly not to be copied), and he wears it plain in 8.1 on the same page. His chain of office has also become a heavy chain with a large conch medallion, unlike the round-link chain with a small pendant in 8.1. Everything else works: Padmini with stick and grey-threaded black hair, Nagoji's face, stud, knife and forearm marks, Revathi in indigo with coins and jasmine, and the sky band for the balloons.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's mundu and shoulder cloth are plain cream cotton with NO gold border, NO kasavu stripe and no coloured edge anywhere, exactly as he wears them in panel 8.1 on this page. His silver chain of office is the same as in 8.1: a chain of small round silver links with a small round pendant on the chest, not a heavy chain with a large conch medallion. Keep everything else as it is: Padmini at frame left walking in with her long stick, in her cream gold-bordered sari with grey-threaded black hair coiled at the nape; Nagoji at the centre beside the carved post, one hand on the rail, black topknot with a touch of grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, the conch-marked ivory knife at his waist and the brand and white scar on his inner left forearm; Revathi at frame right in indigo with jasmine and the flat-coin necklace; the low sun over the sea; and the open sky band across the top for three balloons.

decisions.issues: Nagoji's brand is drawn as a crisp, dark-outlined conch-shell symbol, like a tattoo, on the back of the forearm. The bible locks it as a pale puckered patch of raised ridges, blurred past reading, with no legible shape, on the INNER left forearm. A clear conch also reads as the Travancore emblem rather than a Portuguese slave brand, and it clashes with the conch mark on his knife. The cloth at frame right also has a gold edge stripe, against the plain-mundu lock. The hand count, the touch, the nails, the bangles and the sky for the captions are all good.
decisions.correction: The Portuguese brand on Nagoji's LEFT forearm is NOT a drawn symbol, tattoo or outline. Draw it as a pale, puckered patch of raised, shiny scar ridges about the size of a coin: old burned marks blurred past reading, with no recognisable shape, no conch or shell, no letters, no numerals and not a cross. Set it just above the wrist on the INNER (palm-side) edge of the forearm, turning his forearm slightly outward on the rail so that edge shows while the back of his hand stays uppermost; the long thin white scar runs beside it toward the elbow. The cloth at frame right is his plain cream mundu with no gold border. Keep everything else: the low sun over the sea, the timber rail, Revathi's bangled hand entering from frame left with her fingertips brushing the back of his hand, his ridged, discoloured nails, the fold of gold-bordered indigo sari at frame left, and the open sky across the top for two captions.

decisions.issues: Only candidate v01 is rejected. Revathi has no blouse here: bare shoulders, with the armlets on bare upper arms. That breaks her sheet and the panels on either side (8.1 to 8.4, 9.1 and 9.3 all show the fitted short-sleeved blue blouse), so her costume would change in the middle of the scene. Nagoji has visible stubble on his chin and jaw, which the bible forbids outside captivity. There is also a stray reddish blotch on his outer upper left arm and a white scar on the outer forearm near the elbow, but the bible puts the brand and scar on the INNER left forearm above the wrist. Everything else works: the verandah and sunset match, Padmini watches from the left with her stick, Nagoji has the topknot, flush ear stud, plaque chain and ivory knife, and the hands are sound.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, sunset light, verandah, sea and palms, Padmini at the left with her walking stick watching them, and Nagoji's pose, topknot, flush gold ear stud, silver plaque chain with round medallion and ivory-handled knife unchanged. Fix three things. First, Revathi wears the same fitted short-sleeved deep-blue blouse as on her sheet and in the neighbouring panels, with the gold armlets over the sleeve hems and the gold-bordered indigo pallu over her shoulder. Her shoulders and upper arms are not bare. Second, Nagoji's chin and jaw are smooth and completely clean-shaven, with no stubble or five-o'clock shadow, so only the thick curled moustache shows. Third, remove the reddish mark from Nagoji's upper left arm and the white scar line from his outer left forearm near the elbow, so that arm shows plain smooth skin. His brand and long white scar sit on the INNER left forearm above the wrist, which is turned down to the rail and hidden in this pose.

decisions.issues: Minor issue: the silver chain on Nagoji in the foreground is a plain beaded chain, not the plaque-link chain of office seen in 8.x, but only a short length shows. Otherwise clean. Revathi matches her sheet (blouse, coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line, jasmine braid). In the foreground Nagoji has the black topknot with the same touch of grey as page 8, a flush gold ear stud, the moustache tip, a cream shoulder cloth and no turban. Hands are sound, and the upper-right sky leaves plenty of room for both balloons.

Only candidate v01 is rejected. Nagoji's earring is a gold bead hanging below the lobe, not the small flush stud the author ruled on 2026-10-02 must be enforced in selection. There is also visible stubble on his jaw and chin. His chain of office is a string of large round rings, not the plaque-link chain with round medallion on the verandah pages, and his shoulder cloth has a green-and-gold stripe that differs from 9.2. Everything else works: the night room, clay lamp, low board, brass ink pot, faint-stroke paper, the large shadow on the wall and the open wall space for the captions.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact night room, camera angle and lighting: the clay oil lamp at front left on its brass tray, the low writing board with faint-stroke sheets and the small brass ink pot, the woven mat, the window with night palms at left, the doorway at right, Nagoji cross-legged writing, and his large shadow on the plain wall. Fix the following. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small round gold STUD sitting flush on the earlobe, with nothing hanging below the lobe. His chin and jaw are smooth and completely clean-shaven, with no stubble or shadow, so only the thick curled moustache shows. The silver chain of office matches the verandah panels: small linked rectangular silver plaques ending in a round silver medallion on his chest, not large round rings or beads. His shoulder cloth is cream with gold stripe borders only, with no green stripe. The pen is a plain cut-reed kalam with no metal nib.

decisions.issues: Minor issues. The guard's head is cropped at the top edge (only his bearded mouth shows), so both tails point to the top edge. The room is seen from a reverse angle, with the door at left and the window at right. The lamp stands on a wooden block in the foreground rather than on the brass tray beside the board as in 9.4, and the writing board is shown unattended. Still acceptable: the script beat is clear (a bare-chested Nair guard in a white mundu, his fist knocking at the door frame, the lamp lit in the foreground at night), the board, ink pot, chest, rolled mat and night window are consistent with 9.4, the papers show only faint strokes with no letters, and the large plain wall gives the two GUARD lines plenty of room.

Minor: Nagoji wears a short-sleeved cream tunic under his shoulder cloth. In 9.2, 9.4, 10.2, 10.4 and 10.5 he is bare-chested in the shoulder cloth, so his costume is inconsistent across the page. Otherwise the panel is on model. Nagoji has his topknot, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold stud, silver chain and ivory knife, and stands in the doorway onto the night verandah. Ibrahim (white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat, vest pockets) holds the brass cup. Ramayyan is clean-shaven with receding curly hair, bent over his leaf with a stylus. Hands are sound and there is no text. The plain upper wall between the window and the doorway (x 0.35 to 0.65, y 0 to 0.28) holds both short lines.

Ibrahim's scar is on the wrong side. The thin pink line runs from his RIGHT ear (viewer's left) down into the beard, and his LEFT cheek, which faces Nagoji and the camera's far side, is unmarked. The beat of this panel is the anatomical-left scar turned to the lamp and to us, and 10.3 has it on the left, so this is a mirror-image continuity error. Also, Nagoji in the foreground is sharp, not soft. Everything else works: the room, the lamp, Ibrahim's costume and gesture, Nagoji's bare back with shoulder cloth, his topknot, grey temple and gold stud, and clear wall space for the lettering.
decisions.correction: The scar is on the wrong side: in the last attempt it ran down Ibrahim's RIGHT cheek (viewer's left) because his head was turned toward the right of the frame. Restage as a reverse angle. Put Nagoji's bare shoulder, cream shoulder cloth and black topknot (first grey at the temple, small gold ear stud) slightly out of focus in the near LEFT foreground, his back to us. Seat Ibrahim on the low stool at centre-right, his head turned a little toward the LEFT of the frame to hold Nagoji's eyes, so that his LEFT cheek, LEFT ear and LEFT jaw face the camera. Place the brass oil lamp on the RIGHT side of the frame, close to him, lighting that left cheek. Draw the scar as a thin pale line from just below his LEFT ear down across the cheek to the jawline, clearly visible in the lamplight, and leave his RIGHT cheek unmarked. Keep everything else that worked: the same lamplit plastered room with the lattice window at night and the palm-leaf bundles on the mat; Ibrahim's white turban, short grey-flecked beard, muted-teal short coat over the pale buttoned vest with bulging pockets, striped shoulder cloth and white mundu; his open-palm explaining gesture; and a plain, low-detail stretch of wall above and beside his turban for three lettering lines.

decisions.issues: An unscripted, off-model second figure sits cross-legged at the right with a leaf and stylus. He has a full grey beard and grey hair in a bun, so he matches neither Ramayyan's sheet (clean-shaven, receding black curly hair) nor anyone in the cast. He reads as a new character, or as a bearded, greying Nagoji, while Nagoji is meant to be off-panel. The panel's cast is Ibrahim alone. Ibrahim himself works: he stands by the brass lamp on the shelf, his cup is on the stool, the open door shows the night verandah, the faint scar is on his anatomical left, and his hands are sound.
decisions.correction: Ibrahim Marakkar is the ONLY person in this panel. There is no seated scholar or bearded old man, no Ramayyan, no Nagoji and no other figure anywhere in the frame. Nagoji speaks from off-panel. The right side of the room shows only stacked palm-leaf bundles, a woven basket and plain lamplit plastered wall, kept low-detail for three lettering lines. Keep everything else that worked: Ibrahim standing at the left beside the small brass oil lamp on the wall shelf, his brass cup set down on the round wooden stool beside him, his open right palm turned up as he answers and his left hand at his coat front; his white turban, short grey-flecked beard, muted-teal short coat over the pale buttoned vest with bulging pockets, striped shoulder cloth and white mundu; the thin pale scar from his LEFT ear to the jaw; and the open wooden door behind him onto the dark verandah, the pillar and the night palms.

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. In the main image Ramayyan's stylus is still on the leaf rather than clearly paused, and Nagoji's jaw has a faint shading that still reads as clean-shaven. Everything else matches the script. The doorway is empty with the night beyond, and the brass cup sits on the stool. Nagoji looks down at the cup: topknot, grey temple, thick curled moustache, gold stud, silver chain, bare-armed in his cream shoulder cloth, consistent with 10.2 and 10.5. Ramayyan is on model at his leaf. The lower-right inset shows his hand with the stylus and faint incised marks too fine to read. Hands are sound and there is no text. The plain wall at upper right (x 0.55 to 0.87, y 0 to 0.28) holds Ramayyan's two lines, and the wall above Nagoji, between the window and the door lintel, holds 'You trust him?'.

Minor issues only. The silver chain is thinner than in 10.1, and the paper on the writing board shows faint, illegible strokes, which the script allows. Everything else matches the script. It is night, and Nagoji is seen from behind at his open window, his lost profile showing the moustache and gold stud. His topknot has grey at the temple, and he wears his cream shoulder cloth with a gold border. The lamp stands in the foreground behind him, its flame streaming back into the room away from the window. Inland, dark hills lie under stars with a faint haze. Palm fronds lean toward the window, and the ivory knife hangs on the wall. The starry sky between his head and the palm fronds (x 0.44 to 0.65, y 0.02 to 0.3) and the upper left wall hold the three captions.
